source.title: Base Models Know How to Reason, Thinking Models Learn When
source.authors: Constantin Venhoff; Iv'an Arcuschin; P. Torr; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAEs to reasoning activations in LLMs and reports feature recoverability and stability, providing indirect evidence in an LLM setting rather than reproducing toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE taxonomy stability and human validation of category labels, which bear on whether dictionaries recover stable, interpretable features. Hybrid reasoning-performance results are excluded: the steering is deliberately induced and does not measure naturally occurring superposition. The taxonomy grid-search scores do not measure superposition or canonicality.
record.test_reason: The study uses small Top-K SAEs (5–50 latents, far below the input dimension; the authors call it 'subspace clustering') as a tool to build reasoning taxonomies for model diffing. The seed-stability and human-label checks validate the authors' own clustering method. They are not tests of superposition, of sparse-feature recovery in an overcomplete dictionary (V4), or of dictionary features being the model's canonical units (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The main conclusion is that RL-trained thinking models mainly learn when to deploy reasoning mechanisms already present in the base model (~76% gap recovery), while SFT distillation also installs new mechanisms (~11%). The stability and human-validation results are presented as support for their taxonomy method, not as claims about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sentence-level Top-K SAEs to discover reasoning categories and evaluates their stability and interpretability; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-stability result is for the ORZ-7B SAE at layer 16 with dictionary size 15; decoder-vector cosine similarity was reported as consistently near 1.0 across configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: An undercomplete 15-latent Top-K SAE on sentence-averaged activations matched 93.3% of features across seeds (mean cosine 0.886). The authors contrast this with ~30% reported for large SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature stability across seeds depends on dictionary size: small, undercomplete dictionaries are highly seed-stable.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE decoder vectors had cosine similarity near 1.0 across configurations, so the authors dropped this as an independence metric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder-vector cosine discriminates poorly between these sentence-level SAE taxonomies.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The feature-stability experiment is limited to one ORZ-7B SAE configuration. Human label validation uses one annotator and 15 categories. The paper does not establish that its taxonomies are complete or canonical units of the model's representation.
record.rows_left_out: Hybrid performance and ablation results were left out because steering deliberately induces reasoning behavior rather than measuring naturally occurring superposition. Taxonomy grid-search scores were left out because they assess taxonomy quality, not superposition or canonical feature units.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
No overcomplete dictionary or feature-spread analysis; the SAEs are deliberately undercomplete clusterers.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicality for overcomplete SAE dictionaries.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's labelling of V4/V5 as tested over-reads method-validation checks. The SAEs are explicitly undercomplete (dictionary 5–50 versus a hidden size of thousands) and are used for clustering, so they fall outside the superposition and dictionary-learning regime the versions describe. Steering and hybrid-model results are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse-feature storage in toy networks, feature competition, sparsity-dependent transitions, or superposition geometry.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE-recoverable reasoning categories in the studied models, not feature spread across neurons or LLM representations generally.
Tests stability and human interpretability of a limited reasoning taxonomy; does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units of a model's representation.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features as the units of superposition.

rows.subject: Open-Reasoner-Zero-7B SAE
rows.operation_detail: Matched SAE features across five random-seed runs using the Hungarian algorithm on cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Feature-matching rate (cosine > 0.7) and mean pairwise cosine, averaged across ten seed comparisons.
rows.value: 93.3% average feature-matching rate; mean pairwise cosine 0.886
rows.note: Aggregate across all ten seed comparisons; the paper says the runs had early stopping between epochs 17 and 35.
rows.check: Seed stability of one undercomplete 15-latent SAE on sentence-averaged ORZ-7B activations. This validates the authors' own clustering method; it does not measure V5's overcomplete dictionary features. Moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2.5; Appendix A.1, Table 3: ORZ-7B, layer 16, dictionary size 15, seeds 1–5; overall matching rate 93.3% and mean cosine 0.886 across ten comparisons.

rows.subject: ORZ-7B SAE taxonomy and human annotator
rows.operation_detail: Compared human-written category titles and descriptions with LLM-generated labels for the 15 ORZ-7B categories.
rows.value: 53% (8/15) exact matches, 40% (6/15) partial matches, and 7% (1/15) disagreement; 14/15 full or partial agreement
rows.locator: Appendix C, Human Validation of LLM Judges
rows.note: The paper describes the result as validation of category quality; this does not establish that the taxonomy is complete or canonical.
rows.check: One human annotator's agreement with LLM-generated labels for 15 categories. This validates the method's labelling step; it does not bear on feature recovery or canonicality.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix C, category-label validation: one human annotator; 53% (8/15) exact, 40% (6/15) partial, 7% (1/15) disagreement; 14/15 full or partial agreement.

rows.subject: SAE decoder weight vectors across configurations
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between SAE decoder weight vectors as an orthogonality metric.

conditions.value: different configurations; specific configurations not stated

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between decoder weight vectors
rows.note: The authors say this had limited power to discriminate between taxonomies and instead adopted semantic orthogonality.
rows.check: This is a discarded evaluation metric; the value is only qualitative ('near 1.0'). The link to 'none' is correct.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.5: decoder-vector cosine similarities consistently near 1.0 across different SAE configurations; semantic orthogonality adopted instead.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study uses SAE representations without testing the catalog's superposition claims; its stability and annotation checks evaluate its own taxonomy.

tranche.reason: Small sentence-level SAEs serve as a clustering tool for reasoning taxonomies and model diffing. The listed results validate that method rather than test a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The SAEs have 5–50 latents, far fewer than their input dimensions. These method-validation results do not establish the completeness, stability or canonicality of overcomplete SAE dictionaries.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The SAE categories show high cross-seed matching and mostly full or partial human-label agreement, supporting recoverable reasoning features in this tested setting (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ORZ-7B SAE features, layer 16, dictionary size 15
reader_labels.reason: The reported cross-seed matching and label agreement support stability and interpretability for this taxonomy, but do not establish completeness or canonicality (R1, R2).
